vsm2.17:220.1:
As to the clause “With the sixfold base as condition, contact”:

> Contact is briefly of six kinds
> With eye-contact and others too;
> According to each consciousness
> It is in detail thirty-two.
vsm2.17:221.1: Briefly, with the clause “With the sixfold base as condition, contact,” there are only the six kinds beginning with eye-contact,
vsm2.17:221.2: that is to say, eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact.
vsm2.17:221.3: But in detail the five profitable resultant and the five unprofitable resultant beginning with eye-contact make ten;
vsm2.17:221.4: the rest, which are associated with the twenty-two kinds of mundane resultant consciousness, make twenty-two.
vsm2.17:221.5: So all these come to thirty-two ((34)–(65)), like the consciousness with formations as condition given above.
vsm2.17:222.1: But as to the sixfold base that is a condition for this thirty-twofold contact. Herein:
vsm2.17:222.2:
> Some wise men take the sixfold base
> To be the five internal bases
> With the sixth; but others count
> These plus the six external bases.
vsm2.17:223.1:
Herein, firstly, there are those who take this to be an exposition of the occurrence of what
is clung to, that is, kammically-acquired aggregates,
vsm2.17:223.2:
and they maintain that the conditioning bases and the conditionally-arisen contact
are only what is included in one’s own continuity.
vsm2.17:223.3:
They take any one part to represent any remaining one of its kind, since the condition for contact in the immaterial
states is the sixth base only, according to the text “With the sixth base as condition, contact” (Vibh 179),
vsm2.17:223.4: and elsewhere it is the sixfold base inclusively.
vsm2.17:223.5: So they have it that “sixfold base” means the internal five beginning with the eye plus the sixth (mind) base.
vsm2.17:223.6: For that sixth base and that sixfold base are styled “sixfold base.”
vsm2.17:223.7: But there are those who maintain that it is only the conditionally-arisen contact that is contained in a single continuity,
vsm2.17:223.8: while the conditioning bases are contained in separate that is, past continuities as well.
vsm2.17:223.9: They maintain that all and any such bases are a condition for contact, and they include also the six external ones.
vsm2.17:223.10: So they have it that “sixfold base” means the same internal five plus the sixth plus the external ones beginning with visible data.
vsm2.17:223.11: For that sixth base and that partial sixfold base and the sixfold base along with these external ones each representing the rest
vsm2.17:224.1: Here it may be asked: “One kind of contact does not derive from all the bases, nor all the kinds of contact from one base.
vsm2.17:224.2: And yet ‘With the sixfold base as condition, contact’ is said in the singular. Why is that?”
vsm2.17:225.1: Here is the answer: It is true that neither is one derived from all nor all from one.
vsm2.17:225.2: However, one is derived from many.
vsm2.17:225.3:
For eye-contact is derived from the eye base, from the visible-data base, from the mind base reckoned
as eye-consciousness, and from the mental-datum base consisting of the remaining associated states.
vsm2.17:225.4: And each case should be construed as appropriate in this way.
vsm2.17:225.6:
> Though stated in the singular,
> He shows therewith in all such cases
> That this contact, though only one,
> Is yet derived from several bases.
vsm2.17:225.7: Though stated in the singular: the meaning is, by this statement in the singular that “With the sixfold base as condition, contact,”
vsm2.17:225.8: it is pointed out by the Blessed One (Tādin) that contact, which is of one kind, comes into being from many bases.
vsm2.17:226.1:
How the Sixfold Base is a Condition for Contact

But as regards these bases:
vsm2.17:226.2:
> Five in six ways; and after that
> One in nine ways; the external six
> As contact’s conditionality
> According to each case we fix.
vsm2.17:227.1: Here is the explanation: firstly, the five consisting of the eye base, etc.,
vsm2.17:227.2:
are conditions in six ways, as support, prenascence, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance
conditions, for contact classed in five ways as eye-contact, and so on.
vsm2.17:227.3: After that, the single resultant mind base
vsm2.17:227.4:
is a condition in nine ways, as conascence, mutuality, support, result, nutriment, faculty, association,
presence, and non-disappearance conditions, for the variously-classed resultant mind contact.
vsm2.17:227.5: But in the case of the external bases, the visible-data base
vsm2.17:227.6: is a condition in four ways, as object, prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions, for eye-contact.
vsm2.17:227.7: Likewise the sound base, etc., respectively for ear-contact, and so on.
vsm2.17:227.8: But these and mental data as object are conditions likewise, and as object condition too, for mind-contact,
vsm2.17:227.9: so “the external six as contact’s conditionality according to each case we fix.”
vsm2.17:227.10: This is the detailed explanation of the clause “With the sixfold base as condition, contact.”
vsm2.17:228.1:
As to the clause “With contact as condition, feeling”:

> Feelings, when named by way of door
> “Eye-contact-born” and all the rest,
> Are only six; but then they are
> At nine and eighty sorts assessed.
vsm2.17:229.1:
In the analysis of this clause in the Vibhaṅga only six kinds of feeling according to door are given thus,
“Eye-contact-born feeling, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, mind-contact-born feeling” (Vibh 136).
vsm2.17:229.2:
Still, when classed according to association with the eighty-nine kinds of consciousness,
they are “at nine and eighty sorts assessed.”
vsm2.17:230.1:
> But from the nine and eighty feelings
> Thirty-two, no more, appear
> Associated with result,
> And only those are mentioned here.
vsm2.17:230.2:
> Herein, contact in the five doors
> Conditions five in eightfold way,
> And single way the rest; it acts
> In the mind door in the same way.
vsm2.17:231.1: Herein, in the five doors contact beginning with eye-contact
vsm2.17:231.2:
is a condition in eight ways, as conascence, mutuality, support, result, nutriment, association, presence, and non-disappearance
conditions, for the five kinds of feeling that have respectively eye sensitivity, etc., as their physical basis.
vsm2.17:231.3: But that contact beginning with eye-contact is a condition in one way only, as decisive-support condition,
vsm2.17:231.4: for the rest of resultant feeling in the sense sphere occurring in each door as receiving, investigation and registration.
vsm2.17:232.1: In the mind door in the same way: the contact called conascent mind-contact
vsm2.17:232.2: is also a condition in the same eight ways for sense-sphere resultant feeling occurring as registration in the mind door,
vsm2.17:232.3: and so also for the kinds of resultant feeling in the three planes occurring with rebirth-linking, life-continuum and death.
vsm2.17:232.4: But the mind-contact associated with mind-door adverting is a condition in one way only, as decisive-support condition,
vsm2.17:232.5: for the kinds of feeling that occur in the mind door as registration in the sense sphere.
vsm2.17:232.6: This is the detailed explanation of the clause “With contact as condition, feeling.”
vsm2.17:233.1:
As regards the clause “With feeling as condition, craving”:

> Six cravings, for things visible
> and all the rest, are treated here;
> And each of these, when it occurs,
> Can in one of three modes appear.
vsm2.17:234.1:
Six kinds of craving are shown in the analysis of this clause in the Vibhaṅga, called after their objects,
as a son is called after his father “banker’s son,” “brahman’s son,”
vsm2.17:234.2: namely, “visible-data craving, sound, odour, flavour, tangible-data, and mental-data craving” (Vibh 136).
vsm2.17:234.3: Each of these six kinds of craving is reckoned threefold according to its mode of occurrence
vsm2.17:234.4: as craving for sense desires, craving for becoming, or craving for non-becoming.
vsm2.17:235.1:
When visible-data craving occurs enjoying with sense-desire enjoyment a visible
datum as object that has come into the focus of the eye,
vsm2.17:235.2: it is called craving for sense desires.
vsm2.17:235.3:
But when that same visible-data craving occurs along with the eternity view that assumes that same
object to be lasting and eternal, it is called craving for becoming;
vsm2.17:235.4: for it is the greed accompanying the eternity view that is called craving for becoming.
vsm2.17:235.5:
When it occurs along with the annihilation view that assumes that same object to break
up and be destroyed, it is called craving for non-becoming;
vsm2.17:235.6: for it is the greed accompanying the annihilation view that is called craving for non-becoming.
vsm2.17:235.7: So also in the case of craving for sounds, and so on.
vsm2.17:235.8: These amount to eighteen kinds of craving.
vsm2.17:235.9:
The eighteen with respect to one’s own visible data (one’s own appearance), etc., and eighteen with respect to external
visible data (another’s appearance), etc., together make thirty-six kinds.
vsm2.17:235.10: Thirty-six in the past, thirty-six in the future, and thirty-six in the present, make one-hundred-and-eight kinds of craving.
vsm2.17:235.11: When these are reduced again, they should be understood to amount to the six kinds only with visible data, etc., as object;
vsm2.17:235.12: and these, to three only, as craving for sense desires, and so on.
vsm2.17:236.1:
Out of selfish affection for feeling after taking pleasure in it when it arises through a visible datum
as object, etc., these beings accord much honour to painters, musicians, perfumers, cooks, weavers,
distillers of elixirs, physicians, etc., who furnish respectively visible data as object, etc.,
just as out of affection for a child they reward the child’s nurse after taking pleasure in the child.
vsm2.17:236.2: That is why it should be understood that these three kinds of craving have feeling as their condition.
vsm2.17:237.1:
> What is intended here is but
> Resultant pleasant feeling; hence
> ’Tis a condition in one way
> For all this craving’s occurrence.
vsm2.17:237.2: In one way: it is a condition as decisive-support condition only.
vsm2.17:238.1:
Or alternatively:

> A man in pain for pleasure longs,
> And finding pleasure, longs for more;
> The peace of equanimity
> Is counted pleasure too; therefore
vsm2.17:238.2:
> The Greatest Sage announced the law
> “With feeling as condition, craving,”
> Since all three feelings thus can be
> Conditions for all kinds of craving.
vsm2.17:238.3:
> Though feeling is condition, still
> Without inherent tendency
> No craving can arise, and so
> From this the perfect saint is free.
vsm2.17:238.4: This is the detailed explanation of the clause “With feeling as condition, craving.”
vsm2.17:239.1:
As regards the clause “With craving as condition, clinging”:

> Four clingings need to be explained
> (1) As to analysis of meaning,
> (2) As to the brief and full account
> Of states, (3) and also as to order.
vsm2.17:240.1:
Herein, this is the explanation: firstly, there are these four kinds of clinging here, namely,
sense-desire clinging, false- view clinging, rules-and-vows clinging, and self-doctrine clinging.
vsm2.17:241.1:
The analysis of meaning is this: it clings to the kind of sense-desire called sense-desire’s
physical object (see Ch. IV, n. 24), thus it is sense-desire clinging.
vsm2.17:241.2: Also, it is sense-desire and it is clinging, thus it is sense-desire clinging.
vsm2.17:241.4: for here the prefix upa has the sense of firmness, as in upāyāsa (great misery—see §48) and upakuṭṭha (great pox), and so on.
vsm2.17:241.5: Likewise, it is false view and it is clinging, thus it is false- view clinging;
vsm2.17:241.6: or, it clings to false view, thus it is false- view clinging;
vsm2.17:241.7:
for in the case of the false view “The world and self are eternal” (D I 14), etc.,
it is the latter kind of view that clings to the former.
vsm2.17:241.8: Likewise, it clings to rite and ritual, thus it is rules-and-vows clinging;
vsm2.17:241.9: also, it is rite and ritual and it is clinging, thus it is rules-and-vows clinging;
vsm2.17:241.10:
for ox asceticism, ox vows, etc. (see M I 387f.), are themselves kinds of clinging, too,
because of the misinterpretation (insistence) that purification comes about in this way.
vsm2.17:241.11: Likewise, they indoctrinate by means of that, thus that is doctrine; they cling by means of that, thus that is clinging.
vsm2.17:241.12: What do they indoctrinate with? What do they cling to? Self.
vsm2.17:241.13: The clinging to doctrines of self is self-doctrine clinging.
vsm2.17:241.14: Or by means of that they cling to a self that is a mere doctrine of self; thus that is self-doctrine clinging.
vsm2.17:241.15: This, firstly, is the “analysis of meaning.”
vsm2.17:242.1:
But as regards the brief and full account of states, firstly, in brief sense-desire clinging is called
“firmness of craving” since it is said: “Herein, what is sense-desire clinging?
vsm2.17:242.2:
That which in the case of sense desires is lust for sense desires, greed for sense desires,
delight in sense desires, craving for sense desires, fever of sense desires, infatuation with sense desires,
committal to sense desires: that is called sense-desire clinging” (Dhs §1214).
vsm2.17:242.3:
“Firmness of craving” is a name for the subsequent craving itself, which has become
firm by the influence of previous craving, which acts as its decisive-support condition.
vsm2.17:242.4:
But some have said: Craving is the aspiring to an object that one has not yet reached,
like a thief’s stretching out his hand in the dark;
vsm2.17:242.5: clinging is the grasping of an object that one has reached, like the thief’s grasping his objective.
vsm2.17:242.6:
These states oppose fewness of wishes and contentment and so they are the roots of the suffering
due to seeking and guarding (see D II 58f.).
vsm2.17:242.7: The remaining three kinds of clinging are in brief simply false view.
vsm2.17:243.1:
In detail, however, sense-desire clinging is the firm state of the craving described above
as of one-hundred-and-eight kinds with respect to visible data and so on.
vsm2.17:243.2: False- view clinging is the ten-based wrong view,
vsm2.17:243.3:
according as it is said: “Herein what is false- view clinging? There is no giving, no offering, … no good and virtuous
ascetics and brahmans who have themselves realized by direct-knowledge and declare this world and the other world:
such view as this … such perverse assumption is called false-view clinging” (Vibh 375; Dhs §1215).
vsm2.17:243.4: Rules-and-vows clinging is the adherence to the view that purification comes through rules and vows,
vsm2.17:243.5:
according as it is said: “Herein, what is rules-and-vows clinging? … That purification comes through a rite,
that purification comes through a ritual, that purification comes through a rite and ritual:
such view as this … such perverse assumption is called rules-and-vows clinging” (Dhs §1216).
vsm2.17:243.6: Self-doctrine clinging is the twenty-based false view of individuality,
vsm2.17:243.7:
according as it is said: “Herein, what is self-doctrine clinging? Here the untaught ordinary man … untrained in good
men’s Dhamma, sees materiality as self … such perverse assumption is called self-doctrine clinging” (Dhs §1217).
vsm2.17:243.8: This is the “brief and full account of states.”
vsm2.17:244.1: 3. As to order: here order is threefold (see XIV.211), that is to say, order of arising, order of abandoning, and order of teaching.
vsm2.17:244.2:
Herein, order of arising of defilements is not meant literally because there is no first
arising of defilements in the beginningless round of rebirths.
vsm2.17:244.3:
But in a relative sense it is this: usually in a single becoming the misinterpretation of (insistence
on) eternity and annihilation are preceded by the assumption of a self.
vsm2.17:244.4:
After that, when a man assumes that this self is eternal, rules-and-vows clinging
arises in him for the purpose of purifying the self.
vsm2.17:244.5:
And when a man assumes that it breaks up, thus disregarding the next world, sense-desire
clinging arises in him. So self-doctrine clinging arises first,
vsm2.17:244.6:
and after that, false- view clinging, and rules-and-vows clinging or sense-desire clinging.
This, then, is their order of arising in one becoming.
vsm2.17:245.1: And here false- view clinging, etc., are abandoned first because they are eliminated by the path of stream-entry.
vsm2.17:245.2: Sense-desire clinging is abandoned later because it is eliminated by the path of Arahantship. This is the order of their abandoning.
vsm2.17:246.1:
Sense-desire clinging, however, is taught first among them because of the breadth of its objective
field and because of its obviousness.
vsm2.17:246.2:
For it has a broad objective field because it is associated with eight kinds of consciousness ((22)–(29)).
The others have a narrow objective field because they are associated with four kinds of consciousness ((22), (23), (26) and (27)).
vsm2.17:246.3:
And usually it is sense-desire clinging that is obvious because of this generation’s
love of attachment (see M I 167), not so the other kinds.
vsm2.17:246.4:
One possessed of sense-desire clinging is much given to display and ceremony (see
M I 265) for the purpose of attaining sense desires.
vsm2.17:246.5: False- view clinging comes next to the sense-desire clinging since that display and ceremony is a false- view of his.
vsm2.17:246.6: And that is then divided in two as rules-and-vows clinging and self-doctrine clinging.
vsm2.17:246.7:
And of these two, rules-and-vows clinging is taught first, being gross, because it can
be recognized on seeing it in the forms of ox practice and dog practice.
vsm2.17:246.8: And self-doctrine clinging is taught last because of its subtlety. This is the “order of teaching.”
vsm2.17:247.1:
How Craving is a Condition for Clinging

> For the first in a single way;
> But for the three remaining kinds
> In sevenfold or eightfold way.
vsm2.17:248.1:
As regards the four kinds of clinging taught in this way, craving for sense desires is a condition in one way,
as decisive-support, for the first kind, namely, sense-desire clinging,
vsm2.17:248.2: because it arises in relation to the objective field in which craving delights.
vsm2.17:248.3: But it is a condition in seven ways, as conascence, mutuality, support, association, presence, non-disappearance, and root-cause,
vsm2.17:248.4: or in eight ways, as those and decisive-support as well, for the remaining three kinds.
vsm2.17:248.5: And when it is a condition as decisive-support, then it is never conascent.
vsm2.17:248.6: This is the detailed explanation of the clause “With craving as condition, clinging.”
